clue.text: Fund-raising body wary about appeal

indicators.note: the word for wary goes round, 'about', the other piece

parts.note: it = sex appeal, as in 'she's got it'

explanation.surface: A charity is nervous about launching a fundraising appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' sits so naturally beside a fund-raising body that it reads as a donations drive; it is the old slang sense of allure.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain description: the whole purpose of such an organisation is raising and giving money for a cause.

clue.text: Stop moving in the main?

parts.note: read plainly: come to a standstill
the surface pushes 'mostly'; the setter means 'on the main', the old poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about mostly keeping still.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAVE TO is the sailing term for bringing a ship to a halt at sea, usually by setting the sails against each other; the question mark flags the pun on 'main'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical idiom: to heave to is to stop a vessel while at sea, which is stopping moving on the main.

clue.text: Bachelor interrupting lively dance is one against authority

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A single man barges into a ceilidh and defies the organisers.
explanation.walkthrough: A reel is a fast Scottish country dance, a crossword favourite for four letters meaning dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone who resists or rises against those in charge.

clue.text: Expert on course revised set trip

indicators.note: the letters of SET TRIP are rearranged, as a revised plan is

explanation.surface: A travel expert redoes a planned trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On course' suggests someone on a training course; it means a racecourse, where a tipster advises punters which horse to back.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by setting: the racecourse is where such a person sells supposedly expert predictions of winners.

clue.text: One offering shock treatment?

parts.note: a person who provides a service
the surface pushes electric-shock therapy; a shock is also a thick, bushy mass of hair

explanation.surface: Someone who administers electric shocks as therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'shock' as a mop of hair and the treatment is a cut and blow-dry; the question mark marks the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser's job is treating heads of hair, so a shock of hair is exactly what a stylist works on.

clue.text: Spin to grip each hot drink container

parts.note: ea = each, as on price labels

explanation.surface: Some spin is applied to hold a flask of hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' and 'grip' suggest a tennis or cricket surface, but 'container' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain description: a large heated vessel from which tea is served at church halls and events.

clue.text: Italian is excited to tour restricted centre in northeastern European state

indicators.note: the letters of ITALIAN are stirred up
HUB is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: centre = HUB, restricted to its first two letters

explanation.surface: An Italian gets worked up about a closed-off town centre while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' looks like a middle-letters instruction; it is the synonym HUB, trimmed. 'Is' is part of the surface and joins the fodder to its indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Geographical description: a Baltic state on the northeastern edge of the European Union.

clue.text: Odds on first piece of silver and gold in fund

parts.note: SP = starting price, the odds on a horse at the off

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of 'silver'

explanation.surface: A gambler puts silver and gold coins into a betting fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fund' reads as a noun, a pot of money; it is the verb, to pay for. SP is racing shorthand for the starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to back an event or person with money.

clue.text: Doctor remembers unit for paying back of expenses

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A GP recalls which hospital unit to bill for costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person at the front of the sentence; it is a verb telling you to tamper with the next thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain description: the formal word for repaying money someone has laid out.

clue.text: Minute in scientific site for young farm animal

explanation.surface: A tiny creature is kept in a research lab for a farm animal study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' could be read as 'tiny'; it is the abbreviation for the time unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain description: the young of a sheep.

clue.text: A routine PC changed as safety measure

indicators.note: the letters of A ROUTINE PC are changed round

explanation.surface: A computer's settings are altered to keep it secure.
explanation.walkthrough: PC could be the computer or a police constable; either way it only supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a step taken in advance to guard against harm.

clue.text: Some propel lethal ball of little size

indicators.note: only some of the letters of 'propel lethal' are used

explanation.surface: Someone fires a deadly little ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words; the surface of firing something deadly suits an airgun pellet.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain description: a small round ball, as of lead shot or compressed feed.

clue.text: Brand of car and ship for titled figure

parts.note: a marque is a make of car

explanation.surface: Picking a car make and a boat to suit an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: A marquess is a British noble ranking just below a duke; the car-and-yacht surface suits his wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: one rank of the British peerage, so a person holding a title.

clue.text: Lumbering prince rode on awkwardly with American

indicators.note: the letters of RODE ON are put together awkwardly

explanation.surface: A heavy-footed prince rides clumsily beside an American companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkwardly' fits the lumbering prince in the surface, which hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both describe something heavy, slow and clumsy in movement.

clue.text: European infiltrating field cut out as dishonest

indicators.note: FIELD CUT is put out of order

explanation.surface: A foreign agent sneaks into a mown field and is judged a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut out' looks like one phrase meaning 'removed'; 'cut' belongs to the fodder and 'out' alone says rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: given to lying and misleading others.

clue.text: Criminal nears trap

indicators.note: the letters of NEARS are treated criminally, i.e. wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A crook closes in on an ambush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as a noun, a crook; it is an adjective saying the letters are wrongly arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a noose or device for catching animals.

clue.text: Conventional items kept in a retail outlet?

definitions.meaning: an adjective: standard, routine, as in a hackneyed answer

definitions.text: items kept in a retail outlet
definitions.meaning: a noun: the goods a shop holds for sale

explanation.surface: Asking whether ordinary goods are what a shop keeps.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'stock answer' is a conventional one; a shop's stock is its inventory. The question mark flags the looser second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means standard or routine; the noun means a shop's supply of goods.

clue.text: Sort has no end of scare by house regarding violent storm

indicators.note: the word for sort lacks the letter that follows
take the last letter of 'scare'

parts.words: Sort has no end of scare
parts.note: sort = TYPE, minus E, the end of scare

explanation.surface: A frightened person huddles by the house as a storm rages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regarding' looks like a link to the definition, but it is ON; the definition is only 'violent storm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a tropical cyclone of the western Pacific, the most violent kind of storm.

clue.text: Judges the value of site developed by friends

indicators.note: SITE is developed into a new arrangement

parts.note: mates = friends, placed by the first part

explanation.surface: Pals size up a building plot they are developing.
explanation.walkthrough: The property surface makes 'developed' look like building work; it rearranges SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to form a rough judgement of worth or size.

clue.text: This person's urge to create a favourable impact

explanation.surface: Someone admits their drive to make a good impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person's' means the setter, and the 's is 'is', not a possessive, so it contracts to I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to make people think well of you.

clue.text: Stare at Emily's jacket with fancy label

indicators.note: the letters of LABEL are made fancy, rearranged
a jacket is the outside, so take Emily's outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone gawps at the designer label on Emily's coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The clothing surface makes 'jacket' and 'label' a coat and its tag; the jacket is just the outside of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal idiom: to look someone hard in the eye, a stare.

clue.text: Obstruct part of path in Derbyshire

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the following words

explanation.surface: Something blocks a footpath in the Peak District county.
explanation.walkthrough: Derbyshire is an English county in the Midlands; it is only here to hold letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to get in the way of progress.

clue.text: Tiny chap featured in work is source of memorably cheery outlook

parts.note: Tiny Tim, the boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A small character in a famous work is remembered for his upbeat spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiny Tim, who says 'God bless us, every one!', is the memorably cheery child in Dickens's work, so the surface nearly defines the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain description: a hopeful disposition that expects things to turn out well.

clue.text: Daughter is captivated by strength in fine particles

explanation.surface: A girl is charmed by a show of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captivated' reads as charmed; here it is literal, D taken captive inside the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain description: a substance ground into tiny dry grains.

clue.text: Leaders in western industry dismiss this half-baked range

indicators.note: take the first letters of the next three words
only half of THIS is used

parts.note: first letters of western, industry, dismiss

explanation.surface: Bosses of western firms reject a poorly thought-out product range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dismiss' reads as the bosses' action; it is the third leader. 'Range' is not a product line but breadth, the extent across.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: range as extent or breadth, the measure from side to side.

clue.text: Faith in secret communication

definitions.meaning: a private disclosure, something told on trust

explanation.surface: Someone places their trust in a private message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only joins the two definitions, though it makes the surface read as 'faith in'. Telling someone something 'in confidence' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both trust itself and a secret entrusted to someone.

clue.text: Dull medic is given a book

explanation.surface: A boring doctor is handed something to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull' looks like it describes the medic; it is the definition standing alone at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: lacking colour, brightness or interest.

clue.text: Learnt about second feature of some deer

definitions.note: the definition is singular, the answer plural: a pair of antlers is one feature

indicators.note: the letters are turned about

explanation.surface: Someone studied a second characteristic of deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning'; it rearranges LEARNT with the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: branched bony growths on the heads of male deer, a feature only some have.

clue.text: A special stop to find road surfacing material

explanation.surface: Making an unscheduled stop to look for road-building supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' fits the road surface as a traffic halt, and here it is exactly that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain description: the tarry mixture laid on roads and pavements.
